L00016: L00017: L00022: L00023: L00024: L00025: This is the repo for the InfiAgent project. InfiAgent aims to support building an agent demo from scratch, supporting code execution, API call, batch inference, and sandbox mangagement. You can easily build your own agents based on InfiAgent. L00026: L00027: L00028: L00029: L00030: ## 🔥 News L00031: - 🔥[2024/12/12] Our paper "[OS Agents: A Survey on MLLM-based Agents for General Computing Devices Use](https://os-agent-survey.github.io/)" released. L00032: - [2024/4/2] Our paper on InfiAgent-DABench is accepted by *ICML 2024*. L00033: - [2024/2/21] InfiAgent-DABench and DA-Agent released at [huggingface](https://huggingface.co/infiagent). L00034: - [2024/1/27] [DAEval](https://github.com/InfiAgent/InfiAgent/tree/main/examples/DA-Agent) with human filtering updated. L00035: - [2024/1/10] Our paper on InfiAgent-DABench released on [arxiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05507). L00036: - [2023/12/15] [InfiAgent-DABench](https://github.com/InfiAgent/InfiAgent/tree/main/examples/DA-Agent) released. L00037: - [2023/11/29] InfiAgent repo, and website released. L00038: L00039: ## DA-Agent: An Example Implemented with InfiAgent Framework L00040: We develop [DA-Agent](https://github.com/InfiAgent/InfiAgent/tree/main/examples/DA-Agent), an open-source LLM-based agent for data analysis implemented with InfiAgent framework. L00041: L00042: ## Framework Features L00043: L00044: InfiAgent is a project for building your own agents via code execution and API call. It formulates LLMs as agents via a [REACT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629) pipeline by default. You also can define your own prompt templates. L00045: L00046: L00047: L00048: We have provided a comprehensive pipeline code for running your agent locally. Within the pipeline, we offer API calls, local model inference, a Python code sandbox based on Docker, and a frontend built on Streamlit. We take GPT-3.5 as an example to show how to build a data anaylsis agent given a LLM interface. L00049: L00050: L00051: 1. **API Calls:** L00052: L00053: Simply fill in your API Key, and you can begin making calls to models such as GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claud, and more to run your code interpreter pipeline. L00054: 3. **Local Model Inference:** L00055: L00056: If you would like to run models locally, we've incorporated the capability to perform local inference on your Nvidia GPU. The local inference feature is implemented based on vLLM for optimized performance on your local machine. L00057: 5. **Python Code Sandbox:** L00058: L00059: To execute Python code, we implement a Python code sandbox using a subprocess, which is convenient but may introduce certain security issues. L00060: L00061: Also, we have implemented a Python code sandbox based on Docker, where you can run the pipeline executing the code generated by LLM in an isolated environment without worrying about damage to local files. L00062: L00063: Considering the complexity of the Docker environment configuration, we have set running the sandbox using subprocess as the default option. L00064: 7. **Streamlit-based Frontend:** L00065: L00066: We have provided a front-end based on Streamlit, allowing you to interact with the pipeline in a visualized manner for a clearer and simpler experience. L00067: L00068: # Usage L00069: L00070: ## Installation L00071: L00072: InfiAgent requires **Python version >= 3.9**. L00073: L00074: 1. Install infiagent and requirements L00075: ``` L00076: pip install . L00077: ``` L00078: L00079: 2. You can easily use the following command to start a demo using APIs. You can changes the config s if you need. L00080: ```bash L00081: # Supported LLM: OPEN_AI, AZURE_OPEN_AI, LLAMA, OPT L00082: # api_key is required for API-based models L00083: bash run_demo.sh --llm OPEN_AI --api_key --config_path configs/agent_configs/react_agent_gpt4_async.yaml L00084: ``` L00085: L00086: 3. (Optional) Using docker python sandbox L00087: ```bash L00088: docker build -t codesandbox . L00089: bash run_demo.sh --llm OPEN_AI --api_key --config_path configs/agent_configs/react_agent_gpt4_async_docker.yaml L00090: ``` L00091: L00092: L00093: L00094: ```bash L00095: pip3 install vllm L00096: ``` L00097: ## Demo Usage L00098: L00099: L00100: L00101: ## Run your local model serving L00102: L00103: 1. Our local LLM service is developed on vLLM. First, You should install by command: L00104: L00105: ``` L00106: pip install vllm fschat L00107: ``` L00108: 1. you can start a vLLM model serving by running this command: L00109: L00110: L00111: ```bash L00112: python3 ./activities/vllm_api_server.py --model "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf" --served_model_name "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf" L00113: ``` L00114: At this point, we only support Linux environment. L00115: L00116: 3. You can try this command if the serving is successfully starting: L00117: L00118: ```bash L00119: curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \ L00120: -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ L00121: -d '{ L00122: "model": "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf", L00123: "prompt": "San Francisco is a", L00124: "max_tokens": 7, L00125: "temperature": 0 L00126: }' L00127: ``` L00128: L00129: 4. Then you can run the demo by this command with your local model: L00130: L00131: ```bash L00132: bash run_demo.sh --llm "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf" --config_path configs/agent_configs/react_agent_llama_async.yaml L00133: ``` L00134: L00135: If you run in worker, please change `openai.api_base` in the `./src/infiagent/llm/client/llama.py` to your podIP and then run `pip install .` L00136: L00137: For example, you can change the setting from `"http://localhost:8000/v1"` to `"http://[fdbd:dc03:9:130:5500::e5]:8000/v1"`. L00138: L00139: L00140: L00141: ## Acknowledge L00142: L00143: We would like to express our sincere gratitude to the following open-source projects for their invaluable assistance to our project： L00144: L00145: - [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) L00146: - [FastChat](https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat) L00147: - [Gentopia](https://github.com/Gentopia-AI/Gentopia) L00148: - [autogen](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen) L00149: L00150: L00151: L00152: ## Contact L00153: L00154: If you have any questions, feedback, or would like to collaborate on this project, please feel free to reach out to us through huxueyu@zju.edu.cn. Your inquiries and suggestions are highly appreciated. L00155: L00156: Thank you for your interest in our work! L00157: L00158: L00159: L00160: ## Citation L00161: L00162: If you find our repo useful, please kindly consider citing: L00163: L00164: ``` L00165: @misc{hu2024infiagentdabench, L00166: title={InfiAgent-DABench: Evaluating Agents on Data Analysis Tasks}, L00167: author={Xueyu Hu and Ziyu Zhao and Shuang Wei and Ziwei Chai and Qianli Ma and Guoyin Wang and Xuwu Wang and Jing Su and Jingjing Xu and Ming Zhu and Yao Cheng and Jianbo Yuan and Jiwei Li and Kun Kuang and Yang Yang and Hongxia Yang and Fei Wu}, L00168: year={2024}, L00169: eprint={2401.05507}, L00170: archivePrefix={arXiv}, L00171: primaryClass={cs.CL} L00172: } L00173: ``` L00174:

L00009: # Function to extract formatted text using regular expressions
L00010: def extract_format(input_string):
L00011:     pattern = r"@(\w+)\[(.*?)\]"
L00012:     matches = re.findall(pattern, input_string)
L00013:     answer_names = [match[0] for match in matches]
L00014:     answers = [match[1] for match in matches]
L00015:     return answer_names, answers
L00016: 
L00017: 
L00018: def is_equal(response, label):
L00019:     if response == label:
L00020:         return True
L00021:     else:
L00022:         try:
L00023:             return abs(float(response) - float(label)) < 1e-6
L00024:         except:
L00025:             return False
L00026: 
L00027: 
L00028: # Function to evaluate responses with the adjusted label structure
L00029: def evaluate_responses(labels, responses):
L00030:     results = []
L00031:     for label in labels:
L00032:         label_id = label["id"]
L00033:         label_answers = {ans[0]: ans[1] for ans in label["common_answers"]}
L00034: 
L00035:         corresponding_response = next(
L00036:             (resp for resp in responses if "id" in resp.keys() and resp['response'] and resp["id"] == label_id), None)
L00037:         if corresponding_response:
L00038:             answer_names, answers = extract_format(corresponding_response["response"])
L00039:             extracted_answers = dict(zip(answer_names, answers))
L00040:             correct_answers = {ans_name: is_equal(extracted_answers.get(ans_name), label_answers[ans_name]) for ans_name
L00041:                                in label_answers.keys()}
L00042:             result = {
L00043:                 "id": label_id,
L00044:                 "label_answers": label_answers,
L00045:                 "predicted_answers": extracted_answers,
L00046:                 "correctness": correct_answers
L00047:             }
L00048:             results.append(result)
L00049:     return results
L00050: 
L00051: 
L00052: # Function to read concepts data from a JSONL file
L00053: def read_concepts_from_file(file_name):
L00054:     concepts_data = {}
L00055:     with open(file_name, 'r') as file:
L00056:         for line in file:
L00057:             question_data = json.loads(line.rstrip('\n'))
L00058:             question_id = question_data["id"]
L00059:             concepts = question_data["concepts"]
L00060:             concepts_data[question_id] = concepts
L00061:     return concepts_data
L00062: 
L00063: 
L00064: # Function to analyze concept accuracy
L00065: def analyze_concepts_accuracy(results, concepts_data):
L00066:     concept_accuracy = {}
L00067:     for result in results:
L00068:         question_id = result["id"]
L00069:         if question_id in concepts_data:
L00070:             for concept in concepts_data[question_id]:
L00071:                 if concept not in concept_accuracy:
L00072:                     concept_accuracy[concept] = {"total": 0, "correct": 0}
L00073:                 concept_accuracy[concept]["total"] += 1
L00074:                 if 'correctness' in result and all(result['correctness'].values()):
L00075:                     concept_accuracy[concept]["correct"] += 1
L00076:     return {concept: round(acc["correct"] / acc["total"], 4) for concept, acc in concept_accuracy.items()}
L00077: 
L00078: 
L00079: def analyze_concepts_count_accuracy(results, concepts_data):
L00080:     concept_count_accuracy = {}
L00081:     two_or_more_concepts_accuracy = {"total": 0, "correct": 0}
L00082: 
L00083:     for result in results:
L00084:         question_id = result["id"]
L00085:         if question_id in concepts_data:
L00086:             concept_count = len(concepts_data[question_id])
L00087:             if concept_count not in concept_count_accuracy:
L00088:                 concept_count_accuracy[concept_count] = {"total": 0, "correct": 0}
L00089:             concept_count_accuracy[concept_count]["total"] += 1
L00090: 
L00091:             if 'correctness' in result and all(result['correctness'].values()):
L00092:                 concept_count_accuracy[concept_count]["correct"] += 1
L00093:             if concept_count >= 2:
L00094:                 two_or_more_concepts_accuracy["total"] += 1
L00095:                 if 'correctness' in result and all(result['correctness'].values()):
L00096:                     two_or_more_concepts_accuracy["correct"] += 1
L00097: 
L00098:     concept_count_accuracy = {count: round(acc["correct"] / acc["total"], 4) for count, acc in
L00099:                               concept_count_accuracy.items() if
L00100:                               acc["total"] > 0}
L00101:     if two_or_more_concepts_accuracy["total"] > 0:
L00102:         two_or_more_concepts_accuracy = round(two_or_more_concepts_accuracy["correct"] / two_or_more_concepts_accuracy[
L00103:             "total"], 4)
L00104:     else:
L00105:         two_or_more_concepts_accuracy = None
L00106: 
L00107:     return concept_count_accuracy, two_or_more_concepts_accuracy
L00108: 
L00109: 
L00110: # Functions to evaluate accuracy
L00111: def evaluate_accuracy_by_question(results):
L00112:     correct = sum('correctness' in result and all(result['correctness'].values()) for result in results)
L00113:     total = len(results)
L00114:     return round(correct / total, 4) if total > 0 else 0
L00115: 
L00116: 
L00117: def evaluate_accuracy_by_sub_question(results):
L00118:     correct = sum(sum(result['correctness'].values()) for result in results if 'correctness' in result)
L00119:     total = sum(len(result['correctness']) for result in results if 'correctness' in result)
L00120:     return round(correct / total, 4) if total > 0 else 0
L00121: 
L00122: 
L00123: def evaluate_accuracy_proportional_by_sub_question_adjusted(results):
L00124:     total_score = 0
L00125:     for result in results:
L00126:         if 'correctness' in result:
L00127:             sub_question_count = len(result['correctness'])
L00128:             score_per_sub_question = 1 / sub_question_count if sub_question_count > 0 else 0
L00129:             question_score = sum(result['correctness'].values()) * score_per_sub_question
L00130:             total_score += question_score
L00131:     return round(total_score / len(results), 4) if results else 0
L00132:

L00134: # Main function to run the evaluation
L00135: def main():
L00136:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evaluate closed-form dataset responses.")
L00137:     parser.add_argument('--questions_file_path', type=str, default="data/da-dev-questions.jsonl",
L00138:                         help='Path to the questions file (JSONL format)')
L00139:     parser.add_argument('--labels_file_path', type=str, default="data/da-dev-labels.jsonl",
L00140:                         help='Path to the labels file (JSONL format)')
L00141:     parser.add_argument('--responses_file_path', type=str, required=True,
L00142:                         help='Path to the responses file (JSONL format)')
L00143:     args = parser.parse_args()
L00144: 
L00145:     os.makedirs("eval_outputs", exist_ok=True)
L00146: 
L00147:     # Reading files
L00148:     labels = read_jsonl(args.labels_file_path)
L00149:     responses = read_jsonl(args.responses_file_path)
L00150:     concepts_data = read_concepts_from_file(args.questions_file_path)
L00151: 
L00152:     # Evaluating responses
L00153:     results = evaluate_responses(labels, responses)
L00154: 
L00155:     # Calculate accuracies
L00156:     accuracy_by_question = evaluate_accuracy_by_question(results)
L00157:     accuracy_by_sub_question = evaluate_accuracy_by_sub_question(results)
L00158:     accuracy_proportional_by_sub_question = evaluate_accuracy_proportional_by_sub_question_adjusted(results)
L00159: 
L00160:     # Print results
L00161:     print(f"Accuracy by Question: {accuracy_by_question:.2%}")
L00162:     print(f"Accuracy Proportional by Sub-Question: {accuracy_proportional_by_sub_question:.2%}")
L00163:     print(f"Accuracy by Sub-Question: {accuracy_by_sub_question:.2%}")
L00164:     main_results = {"Accuracy by Question": accuracy_by_question,
L00165:                     "Accuracy Proportional by Sub-Question": accuracy_proportional_by_sub_question,
L00166:                     "Accuracy by Sub-Question": accuracy_by_sub_question}
L00167: 
L00168:     # Analyzing concepts accuracy
L00169:     concept_accuracy_analysis = analyze_concepts_accuracy(results, concepts_data)
L00170: 
L00171:     # Analyzing concepts count accuracy
L00172:     concept_count_accuracy_analysis, two_or_more_concepts_accuracy = analyze_concepts_count_accuracy(results,
L00173:                                                                                                      concepts_data)
L00174: 
L00175:     # Print results
L00176:     print("Concept Accuracy Analysis:")
L00177:     for concept, accuracy in concept_accuracy_analysis.items():
L00178:         print(f"{concept}: {accuracy:.2%}")
L00179: 
L00180:     print("\nConcept Count Accuracy Analysis:")
L00181:     for count, accuracy in concept_count_accuracy_analysis.items():
L00182:         print(f"{count} Concept(s): {accuracy:.2%}")
L00183: 
L00184:     # Print accuracy for questions with >= 2 concepts
L00185:     if two_or_more_concepts_accuracy is not None:
L00186:         print(f"\nAccuracy for Questions with >= 2 Concepts: {two_or_more_concepts_accuracy:.2%}")
L00187:     else:
L00188:         print("\nNo data available for questions with >= 2 Concepts.")
L00189: 
L00190:     responses_file_name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(args.responses_file_path))[0]
L00191:     eval_file_name = f'eval_outputs/{responses_file_name}_evaluation_analysis.json'
L00192: 
L00193:     with open(eval_file_name, 'w') as file:
L00194:         json.dump({
L00195:             "main_results": main_results,
L00196:             "concept_accuracy_analysis": concept_accuracy_analysis,
L00197:             "concept_count_accuracy_analysis": concept_count_accuracy_analysis,
L00198:             "two_or_more_concepts_accuracy": two_or_more_concepts_accuracy
L00199:         }, file, indent=4)
L00200: 
L00201: 
L00202: if __name__ == "__main__":
L00203:     main()

L00070: def extract_questions_and_concepts(file_path):

L00084:         data.append({
